stories.title: Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill – Law Commission
stories.source_name: Law Commission of England and Wales

seen_in.source_name: Law Commission of England and Wales

stories.ltme_summary: The Law Commission of England and Wales says the government has introduced the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill into Parliament. The bill includes measures based on Law Commission recommendations to reinvigorate commonhold and abolish forfeiture. Professor Lisa Webley welcomed the progress.
stories.hook: Government introduces Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill, drawing on Law Commission work
entities: Law Commission of England and Wales

stories.title: Automated vehicles: Who controls the evidence after a collision?
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal article by Michael McCabe, Joanna Folan and Pete Allchorne says automated vehicles will change road traffic litigation because the vehicle's own data may become key evidence. It argues that manufacturers and other third parties will control much of that data, so solicitors must identify custodians and send preservation requests early.
stories.hook: Automated vehicle data will decide liability, and third parties hold much of it

stories.title: SRA proposes SQE changes for candidates
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has opened a consultation on SQE changes that would let candidates sit FLK1 and FLK2 separately, remove attempt limits and start the six-year period after a first pass. The consultation runs from 19 November 2026 to 11 February 2027, with changes intended for 2027.
stories.hook: SRA consults on removing SQE attempt limits and splitting FLK assessments

Judges may soon have to authenticate video evidence in the face of deepfakes. The item is a conference report with no single company deal or ruling.

stories.title: Legora Appoints Former HubSpot, Atlassian Lawyer as Inaugural Chief Legal Officer
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Legora has appointed Erika Fisher, formerly a lawyer at HubSpot and Atlassian, as its first chief legal officer. Fisher will lead the startup's legal team and support product development for in-house departments.
stories.hook: Legora names former HubSpot and Atlassian lawyer Erika Fisher as first chief legal officer

stories.title: Litigation Boutique Offering Bonuses Up To $247K
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports that Pallas Partners, a transatlantic trial boutique founded by Natasha Harrison, has set associate bonuses topping out at $247,000. The firm says this exceeds the $155,000 Cravath pays its most senior associates, with timing to be communicated separately. The item is a compensation story rather than technology.
stories.hook: Pallas Partners tops associate bonuses at $247,000, $92,000 above Cravath's senior figure

It also notes law firm staff views on AI. Each item is a roundup pointer to a third-party report.

Speakers discuss how commercial property can adapt to technology and economic change. Search Acumen's managing director says AI is the most accessible transformative technology since the spreadsheet and warns of slowing deal decisions.

stories.title: Motor injury claims at a decade low: What the shrinking market means for claims firms
stories.ltme_summary: National Claims writes, via Legal Futures, that ACSO figures show 282,428 motor injury claims were registered in 2025, down 14 per cent on 2024 and almost 58 per cent below 2018. The piece links the fall to the 2021 whiplash reforms and raises questions about whether injured motorists still get support.
stories.hook: Motor injury claims fall to 282,428 in 2025, down 14 per cent in a year

stories.title: Nexa Law: A modern post room for a modern legal model
stories.ltme_summary: Nexa Law, a consultancy-model firm with more than 200 partners, describes how it uses Post Partner's Optimum Post Room integrated with its LEAP case management system. Jess Smith, Nexa's COO, says post that once took up to five admin staff now lands automatically on the correct matter, a result the article presents as sponsored content.
stories.hook: Nexa Law says Post Partner's post room integration with LEAP removed manual post handling

stories.title: Why financial discipline is becoming critical for law firm profitability
stories.ltme_summary: Osprey Approach's podcast episode features Mark Adderley of Crowe UK, drawing on Crowe's 2025 Law Firm Benchmarking Report. He says city and regional firms face a widening profitability gap and urges firms to improve time recording, prompt billing and cost control rather than simply adding fee-earning work. The piece is sponsored content relayed by Legal Futures.
stories.hook: Crowe's Mark Adderley says law firms should fix time recording and billing before chasing more fee-earning work

stories.title: How intelligent workflows are transforming the client experience for law firms
stories.ltme_summary: OneAdvanced, writing through Legal Futures, says its Legal Trends Report 2026 finds 62 per cent of firms face a platform integration crisis and 64 per cent are stuck in what it calls automation purgatory. The article argues connected, intelligent workflows improve client experience and that AI works best inside them.
stories.hook: OneAdvanced says 62 per cent of law firms face a platform integration crisis

stories.title: Startup Corner: People’s Court builds an AI disputes platform
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider's Startup Corner profiles People's Court, which is building an AI disputes platform. The extract available is only the site's verification prompt, so the product details, funders and customers cannot be confirmed from it.
stories.hook: Startup Corner profiles People's Court and its AI disputes platform

stories.title: Law firms risk automating away their next generation of lawyers, Supreme Court judge warns
stories.ltme_summary: Lord Sales, a Supreme Court justice, told a conference at DAC Beachcroft's London office that law firms risk losing their future talent pipeline if AI takes over junior work. He argued that lawyers and judges may stop scrutinising AI output and suggested AI could eventually decide lower-value disputes subject to human review.
stories.hook: Lord Sales warns AI could erode the junior training that produces senior lawyers

stories.title: Mayer Brown names six new London partners as global intake dips
Profession welcomes national legal service proposal
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Commons justice committee has called for a national legal service modelled on NHS 111. Law Society president Brett Dixon welcomes the idea but says it cannot replace funded local providers. The Ministry of Justice says it is exploring a national legal service and cites extra legal aid investment.
stories.hook: Justice committee urges a national legal service modelled on NHS 111

stories.title: LiPs allowed to recover cost of AI legal research subscription
stories.ltme_summary: The High Court, in Foster and Another v Wargrave on Thames Housing Association, ruled that two litigants in person can recover the £1,488 cost of an AI legal research subscription as a disbursement. Mr Justice Sweeting said the tool made a real contribution, but stressed that recoverability depends on the facts of each case.
stories.hook: High Court lets litigants in person recover £1,488 AI research subscription costs
entities: Foster & Anor v Wargrave on Thames Housing Association Ltd

stories.title: Forget Impeachment, Just Stop Paying For Todd Blanche’s DOJ
Firms Want AI To Save Hours, Clients Want AI To Save Dollars — They Aren’t The Same Number
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports on Legal Innovators New York, where law firm and in-house tracks diverged on AI. Pillsbury lawyers predicted clients will keep more work in-house and trim outside counsel lists, while in-house attendees pressed firms for cost savings. The column cites an ACC/Everlaw survey finding 59 percent of in-house lawyers saw no noticeable savings from firms' AI use, and an Axiom report on rate-cut expectations.
stories.hook: In-house lawyers want AI savings passed to clients while firms see AI as a way to fill more hours

stories.title: Bob Giuffra Is Handing Off Sullivan & Cromwell. The Trump Baggage Might Be Harder To Hand Off.
Manitoba law society notes loss of almost $1M to payment misdirection
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society of Manitoba has warned that five payment misdirection frauds have hit the province's lawyers over the past two months, with losses of nearly $1m. The regulator said most cases appear to have no insurance cover, and two affected firms lacked trust accounts. Its fraud alert sets out how the scam works and advises lawyers on email security, multifactor authentication and verifying payment instructions by phone.
stories.hook: Manitoba's law society says payment misdirection fraud has cost lawyers nearly $1m, mostly without insurance cover

The extract says access to justice relies too heavily on a patchwork of providers offering early advice, which it describes as insecure and under-resourced. The panel's specific AI arguments are not visible in the extract.

stories.title: DOJ Demand To Hide Misconduct Inside Special Master Fails To Impress Judge
stories.ltme_summary: Judge April Perry in Chicago has rejected a Justice Department request to refer privilege questions in a grand jury misconduct inquiry to a special master or other disinterested officer. Associate Attorney General Stan Woodward made the request after the US Attorney's office in Chicago dismissed charges against the 'Broadview 6'. Judge Perry issued a minute order criticising the government's reliance on case law.
stories.hook: Judge Perry in Chicago turns down DOJ bid to hand privilege rulings in grand jury misconduct inquiry to a special master

stories.title: Biglaw’s ‘Sea Of Sameness’ Is Getting A Million-Dollar Makeover
Court Tells Cops That The 4th Amendment Doesn’t Cover AI-Generated ‘Probable Cause’
stories.ltme_summary: A Kentucky court decision reported by Above the Law holds that the Fourth Amendment does not allow police to rely on an AI facial recognition match alone to establish probable cause. The case concerns Alain Osorio, arrested in Florence, Kentucky, after a Florence Police detective ran a CCTV screenshot through facial recognition and relied on the result. The charges were later dismissed. The commentary links the ruling to wider police use of AI.
stories.hook: Kentucky court rules an AI facial recognition match alone cannot establish probable cause for arrest

stories.title: Phased Fees Can Help Litigators Move Beyond Billable Hours
Legora Hires HubSpot Legal Chief as AI Battle Moves In-House
stories.ltme_summary: Legal AI company Legora has appointed Erika Fisher, formerly Chief Legal Officer at HubSpot, as its first Chief Legal Officer, effective 16 November 2026. Legora says in-house teams made up over 40 per cent of new customers in the third quarter and that it serves more than 2,500 law firms and legal teams in over 80 markets. Fisher previously held legal and operating roles at Atlassian. The role will also help shape Legora's product for corporate counsel.
stories.hook: Legora hires former HubSpot CLO Erika Fisher as first chief legal officer as it targets in-house teams

The headline indicates a practice note for investment advisers and funds on the SEC's examination approach.

stories.title: Legal Automation Software With Human Review: A 2026 Comparison
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic has published a 2026 comparison of legal automation software with human review, arguing that governance of the decision path matters more than a final review step. The post groups tools into document generators such as HotDocs and Contract Express, and no-code workflow builders, and positions Neota Logic as a control layer over tools such as Harvey, ChatGPT and Claude. It cites ABA Formal Opinion 512.
stories.hook: Neota Logic argues legal automation needs governed decision paths, not a final human review button

stories.title: How Can Law Firms Manage Departing Attorney Data and Retention?: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: eDiscovery Today commentary, written by Doug Austin, sets out how law firms can handle data left behind by departing attorneys without keeping every former-user account indefinitely. Shelley Bougnague of Cloudficient argues for separating account closure from the review and governance of client and matter information, which may sit across email, cloud storage and the DMS. The post is sponsored by Cloudficient, an educational partner of the publication.
stories.hook: Cloudficient argues law firms should separate departing-attorney account closure from governance of client data

Group CFO Jane Smith says the aim is shorter lockup through connected time, billing and e-billing systems. The firm, with more than 500 staff across 11 offices, received the Better Together Award at Momentum London, according to the piece.

stories.title: The compliance queue never sleeps. Neither did I.
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp describes a webinar demonstration of Intapp Compliance with Celeste, its AI agent for law firm new business intake and conflicts. The post shows a partner starting a matter request from Outlook, with the agent pre-filling the form for an assistant to review. It also describes automating conflict tasks such as alias checks and sanctions screening.

stories.title: What Fiduciary-Grade AI™ means for Canadian firms: Four questions to ask any AI tool
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters CaseLines sets out four questions small and midsize Canadian firms should put to any legal AI tool, linked to its Fiduciary-Grade AI principles. The post says CoCounsel Legal was designed to answer them, citing curated Canadian content and built-in privacy. It also cites Zhang v. Chen, a 2024 British Columbia decision, and a survey of 1,816 professionals showing 34 per cent use unsanctioned AI tools.
stories.hook: Thomson Reuters offers Canadian firms four questions to test legal AI tools before client files
